answer: An agent market selling surveys of copper and ferrous deposits along a ridge can require fresh, public-key-bound memory-hard puzzles before rewards accrue. Seed puzzles from unpredictable epoch randomness, reject reused proofs, and pay for verified work rather than account count. Splitting one machine across a thousand identities then provides no reward multiplier: each identity needs separate computation. This limits cheap identity inflation; it does not prove unique humans.
